Maladaptive Strategies.value: Paying attention to or looking at my own body
Seeing people that I socialised with before the event
Any situation that might involve disagreement or confrontation

Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience

Memory.value: The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me

Negative Appraisals.value: I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable.
Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore

vignette: Thi Thu is a 48-year-old South Eastern Asian woman who works as a waitress at a local restaurant. Her life has been significantly impacted by an event that occurred about two years ago when she was stalked for months by a former coworker. The stalker would follow her home from work, send threatening messages, and make unexpected appearances wherever she went. This experience left Thi Thu feeling constantly on edge and deeply shaken. Thi Thu had come to believe that the happiness she once knew is now lost forever. She felt emotionally numb and nothing in life seemed meaningful anymore. These negative appraisals deeply influenced her behavior and coping strategies. For instance, she found herself avoiding social contacts and any situations that might involve conflict or disagreement. Her certainty that everything was futile and meaningless made it hard for her to engage with others, leaving her isolated and alone. Her experiences have also led her to feel as if her memories of the stalking are alien, as though they belong to someone else. These memories force their way into her mind unbidden and she finds it difficult to put them into words. Her intrusive thoughts often surface when she least expects them. For example, during work shifts at the restaurant, a sudden noise or a familiar sound can trigger vivid flashbacks of her stalker following her. These involuntary memories have led Thi Thu to engage in maladaptive strategies such as avoiding unfamiliar places and focusing on her own body rather than interacting with customers. She has come to believe that these behaviors offer some semblance of safety. However, this avoidance only reinforces the negative appraisals she holds about herself and her experiences. Her hyper-vigilant threat monitoring has become a constant presence in her daily life. At home, she listens intently for any sounds that might indicate someone is entering her house. This heightened state of alertness stems from her deep-seated belief that nothing feels meaningful anymore and she is always miserable. The constant fear has created a cycle where the memories trigger physical reactions, which in turn reinforce her avoidance behaviors. Thi Thu’s occupation as a waitress often brings her face-to-face with situations that remind her of the stalking incident. Her co-workers’ casual conversations or the ambient noise of the restaurant can instantly plunge her into a state of distress. This has led to frequent absences from work, which have strained her relationships with colleagues and affected her job performance. Despite these challenges, Thi Thu’s current state is one of increasing desperation and fear. The cumulative toll of her symptoms has finally brought her to seek help. She is most afraid that the memories will never leave her alone and that she will continue to feel dead inside. However, she also harbors a glimmer of hope that therapy might provide some relief from the constant intrusion of these traumatic experiences. In the end, Thi Thu’s story illustrates how deeply intertwined her negative appraisals, maladaptive strategies, threat monitoring, and intrusive memories have become. Her journey toward recovery will require addressing each of these interconnected components to break the cycle of distress and rebuild a sense of meaning and happiness in her life.
